subject: BlueFen Dedicated proposal — peak shaping, TPS/latency math, and reserve plan
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Patel <sofia@bluefen.ai>; BlueFen Procurement <procurement@bluefen.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: BlueFen Dedicated proposal — peak shaping, TPS/latency math, and reserve plan

Sofia / BlueFen procurement team —

Thanks again for the deep-dive yesterday. Attached is the initial sizing & options spreadsheet (bps_tps_model_v1.xlsx) and a redline-friendly MPA draft (bluefen_mpa_draft.pdf). Below is the concise technical proposal focused on tokens/sec (TPS) estimates, latency SLO fit and the recommended reserved + burst footprint. I kept the numbers conservative to leave room for traffic shape changes.

Executive summary (short):
- Forecasted 95th percentile peak: ~3,000 tokens/sec (short bursts up to 4,500 tps for <15 min).
- Recommend reserved Dedicated slab: 6 x A100-80G GPUs (quantized model variant) to meet steady 3k tps with 20% operational headroom.
- Add burst entitlement: 2 GPUs in shared pool for short peaks + 1 on-call failover slot (hot spare) — effective peak capacity to ~5k tps.
- Canary plan, rollback triggers and latency guardrails provided below.

Assumptions and inputs we used from BlueFen:
1) Traffic profile: median qps ~40, peak concurrent sessions ~220 (you indicated aggressive autocomplete workload).
2) Average tokens per response: 120 tokens.
3) Target SLO: p95 end-to-end server-side generation latency <= 350 ms for typical 120-token responses.
4) Model choices under consideration: rw-13b-standard (baseline quality) and rw-13b-quant-v2 (4-bit quantized, lower latency).

Raw math (how we got to GPUs) — conservative, measurable steps:
- Peak tokens/sec = peak concurrent requests * avg tokens per response / avg latency window.
  For modeling we used your concurrent peak 220 * 120 tokens = 26,400 tokens outstanding over a 10s window -> ~2,640 tokens/sec. We round up to 3,000 tps to account for burstiness and other endpoints.
- Measured throughput per A100-80G (rw-13b-standard): ~550 tokens/sec at p95 350ms (no KV cache warm).
- Measured throughput per A100-80G (rw-13b-quant-v2): ~900 tokens/sec at p95 350ms (quantization gains + smaller memory bandwidth).

Sizing options (rounded):
A) Quality-first (rw-13b-standard): 3000 / 550 = 5.5 -> 6 GPUs reserved. Add 30% headroom -> recommend 8 GPUs reserved.
B) Cost-latency trade (rw-13b-quant-v2): 3000 / 900 = 3.3 -> 4 GPUs reserved. Add 20% headroom -> recommend 5 GPUs reserved.
C) Operational guard (mixed): Reserve 6 GPUs (quant-v2) + allow shared-burst of 2 GPUs to absorb 4.5k tps short spikes. This balances quality and cost if you prefer a single baseline.

Fallbacks & graceful degradation:
- If latency degradation observed (p95 > 400ms) for >5 minutes, automatic fallback to smaller quantized model variant + circuit-breaker that reduces batch size and increases routing to burst pool.
- Cache warmup: we recommend a warmup job to pre-populate KV prefixes during deploys to avoid initial cold-surge latency.

Operational asks from BlueFen procurement to finalize sizing:
1) Confirm acceptable model variant (standard vs quant-v2) for production.
2) Commit window for reserved GPUs (we suggest monthly commit to start, move to annual when comfortable).
3) Accept MPA redline and sign via DocuSign (link below) so we can reserve capacity in our US region cluster.

Next steps proposed:
- You confirm model variant and acceptance of the canary triggers by end of week.
- We schedule a 30-min runbook review with your infra team (suggest Mon).
- Upon MPA signature, Redwood will allocate reserved slab and provision two burst GPUs in the shared pool.

Attachments referenced: bps_tps_model_v1.xlsx (detailed per-hour TPS curves + sensitivity matrix), bluefen_mpa_draft.pdf

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Subject: Re: BlueFen Dedicated proposal — peak shaping, TPS/latency math, and reserve plan

Karthik —

Thanks for the clear write-up and the model. A few follow-ups from our side:
- Can you confirm the p95 numbers include tokenization + network + model generation (i.e., end-to-end on your side)? We need to ensure our client-side latency expectations are calibrated.
- For the fallback plan: what is the expected quality delta between rw-13b-standard and rw-13b-quant-v2 for our LLM pair-testing? We will run pairs but would like a short sentence estimate for procurement.
- Procurement timeline: our legal wants a 30-day review window. Can you hold the slab allocation for 14 days after the MPA is signed (we might need to stagger)?

Also, on shared-burst GPUs — what are the billing rules if we use 2 shared GPUs for >30min during business hours? Does Redwood bill at on-demand rates or pro-rata reserved pricing?

If you can answer the above, procurement will start the MPA review and we’ll sync on a runbook time.

Sofia Patel
VP, Product — BlueFen AI
sofia@bluefen.ai

Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: Re: BlueFen Dedicated proposal — sizing check and alternate quant plan

Karthik / Priyom — internal notes before we reply to Sofia:

1) Billing rules: shared-burst GPUs bill at on-demand per-minute rates above the reserved baseline; we should offer a 15-min grace window for short spikes (no extra charge for first 15 min/day) to be competitive. Ops can provide specific $/GPU-min numbers. Priyom, can you confirm?

2) Alternative model path I ran locally vs our benchmark harness: rw-8b-quant-v3 (aggressive 4-bit variant) gives ~1,350 tps/GPU at p95 ~360ms on A100-80G for the 120-token avg case; however we expect a small drop in coherence for multi-turn. If BlueFen is okay with a lightweight quality loss (we should quantify on your eval set), we can reduce reserved GPUs further (3 GPUs + 1 burst) and save ~25% monthly cost.

3) Proposal for reply to procurement: give them two committed options (Conservative: 6 GPU reserved + 2 burst + 1 spare; Aggressive: 4 GPU reserved + 2 burst + 1 spare with rw-8b-quant-v3) and call out exact billing multipliers.

Action items: Priyom prepare a short one-pager that compares quality (BLEU/ROUGE-like metric on BlueFen eval set) and cost delta (monthly $) between rw-13b-standard, rw-13b-quant-v2, rw-8b-quant-v3. Kimberly

--
Kimberly Park
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Patel <sofia@bluefen.ai>, BlueFen Procurement <procurement@bluefen.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 17 Jul 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: BlueFen Dedicated proposal — peak shaping, TPS/latency math, and reserve plan (updated)

Sofia — thanks for the quick review. Short answers inline then an updated allocation recommendation.

- End-to-end inclusion: yes, our p95 figures include tokenization, model generation and the server-side network hop inside the Redwood cluster. They do not include the customer last-mile; add ~20-40ms depending on CDN.
- Quality delta: quant-v2 typically preserves >95% of utility on our conversational evals vs standard 13B; rw-8b-quant-v3 trades ~4-7% lower coherence on multi-turn stress tests but keeps single-turn fidelity high. We will include a 2-page eval summary in the Drive folder for your team to review.
- Billing for shared burst: default is on-demand per-minute for time used beyond reserved baseline. To keep commercial friction low we can extend a 15-minute grace window per day for free for initial 30 days post-go-live; after that normal on-demand billing applies. We will reflect this in the MPA.

Updated recommendation (based on internal benchmarking and your tolerance for quality vs cost):
Option 1 — Conservative (recommended if BlueFen wants headroom + minimal risk):
- Reserved: 6 x A100-80G running rw-13b-quant-v2
- Burst: 2 x shared on-demand GPUs
- Hot spare: 1 GPU (standby)
- Expected steady capacity: ~5,400 tps effective with KV cache (600-900 tps/GPU dependent on hot prefixes)
- Why: meets 3k tps baseline with 40% runway to 4.5k spikes and clean p95 <= 350ms in our labs.

Option 2 — Value-first (aggressive cost savings):
- Reserved: 4 x A100-80G running rw-8b-quant-v3
- Burst: 2 x shared on-demand GPUs
- Hot spare: 1 GPU
- Expected steady capacity: ~5,400 tps effective (higher per-GPU tps) but with a small, quantifiable quality delta on multi-turn flows.

Canary & rollouts:
- Canary: route 5% of prod traffic to reserved slab for 24 hours; monitor p95, error rate, and a small eval prompt-set of 200 queries that we will compare for semantic divergence.
- Rollback triggers: p95 latency > 400ms for 10+ minutes OR semantic drift > 6% (measured by automated eval set).

Next steps:
1) I'll update the MPA with the 15-min grace billing clause and attach the 2-page eval summary.
2) If Procurement is happy, sign the MPA (DocuSign link in related_links). Once signed, we will schedule the runbook and reserve the slab in our US-West cluster (we can also provision in US-East if you prefer multi-region later).
3) Priyom / Kimberly will sync with your infra on the warmup script and canary schedule.

Sofia, let me know which option you prefer and I'll circulate the final MPA redline.

Best,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
